correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\geq2\) and real \(a,b>0\), Poisson log-concavity makes each latent pair factor TP2; products and the verified MTP2 marginalization theorem yield the joint MTP2 claim. The bivariate conditional-on-pair-sum mass g(x,s) has a coefficient representation whose adjacent TP2 determinant is a nonnegative sum of two log-concavity differences, proving LR monotonicity for all totals. At full totals n-1 and n, exact Poisson splitting reduces Q to a binomial law and a two-state mixture, giving the if-and-only-if tail transition. In \(n=3\) the exact four-atom probability vectors yield LR iff \(b\leq2a^3\) and ST iff \(b\leq6a^3\). Standalone exact-rational checks passed 28+90 threshold cases, 676 TP2 minors, and 104328 MTP2 inequalities; these finite diagnostics are not substituted for the universal proof.

evidence: Fallat et al., arXiv:1510.01290v2, Section 3 Proposition 3.4(ii), prove closure of MTP2 under marginalization, not conditional ordering under an aggregate sum.

Pellerey & Navarro, DOI 10.1007/s11749-021-00789-5, Proposition 3.1, assumes that (X_i, sum of the other coordinates) itself is logconcave TP2; the present counterexample shows full-vector MTP2 does not imply their sufficient premise.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general MTP2 theorem proves a positive dependence property only, which is a premise, not the claimed negative conditional-order obstruction. Independent-logconcave Efron/Lehmann monotonicity is inapplicable because the X_i share Z. The prior multivariate sufficient condition does not dominate the present statement.

originality.rationale: The inspected Pellerey–Navarro (2021) result gives conditional-order hypotheses via a logconcave TP2 distribution of (X_i, sum of the OTHER coordinates), not via MTP2 of the full vector. It neither reports this shared-Poisson MTP2 conditional-order failure nor the thresholds \(b=2a^3\) and \(b=6a^3\). Schulz–Genest–Mesfioui (2021) provide the classical common-shock model formula, not the new ordering claims. Ellis and Sijtsma (2023) analyze monotonicity given the rest score, which excludes the tested coordinate, a different conditioning statistic. Fallat et al. give the MTP2 closure principle used as known theory. Targeted semantic and bibliographic searches did not identify an implication covering the complete claim; a historically equivalent formulation remains possible.
residual_risks: Earlier equivalent observations in multivariate Poisson actuarial or reliability terminology may have escaped the search; no independent exhaustive priority certification.
The general problem of conditional total ordering at all pairs of sums is deliberately not resolved.

value.rationale: The result identifies the precise failure of Efron-style monotonicity under observation of a full aggregate in a standard, genuinely positively dependent count model. The contrast is structural: the joint vector is MTP2, and every pair remains LR ordered conditional on its pair sum, yet an additional coordinate permits a reverse upper tail. The sharp first-dimension LR/ST gap and explicit general-dimensional threshold directly answer a motivated boundary question left by prior conditional-sum monotonicity investigations. It is not a routine restatement of the known common-shock mass formula or the standard MTP2 closure theorem.
